assumptions.message: The series does not look stationary; difference it (ARIMA does this for you) or remove the trend before modelling.

interpretation.text: The series passengers has 144 observations from 1949 Jan to 1960 Dec. It shows a strong trend (strength 0.97) and moderate seasonality (strength 0.78). The series is not stationary.

title: Time Series Explorer
code:
library(ggnext)
# Time series: passengers (seasonal period 12)
d <- data[!is.na(data$passengers), , drop = FALSE]
d <- d[order(d$date), , drop = FALSE]   # rows in time order
y <- ts(d$passengers, frequency = 12, start = c(1949, 1))
decomp <- stl(y, s.window = "periodic")
components <- as.data.frame(decomp$time.series)
# Strength of trend and seasonality (0 = none, 1 = dominant)
strength <- with(components, c(trend = max(0, 1 - var(remainder, na.rm = TRUE) / var(trend + remainder, na.rm = TRUE)), seasonal = max(0, 1 - var(remainder, na.rm = TRUE) / var(seasonal + remainder, na.rm = TRUE))))
seasonal_tbl <- data.frame(period = as.integer(cycle(y))[seq_len(frequency(y))], effect = components$seasonal[seq_len(frequency(y))])
lags <- min(24, length(y) - 2)
autocorrelation <- data.frame(lag = seq_len(lags), acf = as.numeric(acf(y, lag.max = lags, plot = FALSE)$acf)[-1], pacf = as.numeric(pacf(y, lag.max = lags, plot = FALSE)$acf))
ljung_box <- Box.test(y, lag = lags, type = "Ljung-Box")
# Stationarity: ADF tests H0 = unit root (non-stationary); KPSS tests H0 = stationary
adf <- suppressWarnings(tseries::adf.test(y))     # warns when p is outside the tabulated range
kpss <- suppressWarnings(tseries::kpss.test(y))
series_df <- data.frame(time = as.numeric(time(y)), value = as.numeric(y))
p_series <- ggnext(series_df, aes(time, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Time series of passengers", x = "Time", y = "Passengers (thousands)") +
  theme_modern()
parts <- c("Observed", "Trend", "Seasonal", "Remainder")
decomp_df <- data.frame(time = rep(as.numeric(time(y)), 4), value = c(as.numeric(y), components$trend, components$seasonal, components$remainder),
                        component = factor(rep(parts, each = length(y)), levels = parts))
decomp_df <- decomp_df[!is.na(decomp_df$value), ]
p_decomposition <- ggnext(decomp_df, aes(time, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(vars(component), ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time", y = "Passengers (thousands)") +
  theme_modern()
acf_df <- with(acf(y, lag.max = lags, plot = FALSE), data.frame(lag = as.numeric(lag) * frequency(y), value = as.numeric(acf)))
acf_df <- acf_df[acf_df$lag > 0, ]
acf_df_limit <- qnorm(0.975) / sqrt(length(y))   # limits expected for white noise
p_acf <- ggnext(acf_df, aes(x = lag, y = 0, xend = lag, yend = value)) +
  geom_segment() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = acf_df_limit, dash = "4 4") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -acf_df_limit, dash = "4 4") +
  labs(title = "Autocorrelation (ACF)", x = "Lag", y = "Autocorrelation") +
  theme_modern()
pacf_df <- with(pacf(y, lag.max = lags, plot = FALSE), data.frame(lag = as.numeric(lag) * frequency(y), value = as.numeric(acf)))
pacf_df_limit <- qnorm(0.975) / sqrt(length(y))   # limits expected for white noise
p_pacf <- ggnext(pacf_df, aes(x = lag, y = 0, xend = lag, yend = value)) +
  geom_segment() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = pacf_df_limit, dash = "4 4") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -pacf_df_limit, dash = "4 4") +
  labs(title = "Partial autocorrelation (PACF)", x = "Lag", y = "Partial autocorrelation") +
  theme_modern()
